method: Read each chapter snapshot in full by automated lexical scanning, preserving source line numbers.
Strip comments, control-sequence metadata, inline/display math and native diagram code for English prose candidate detection.
Manually triage all644 high-threshold English-token candidate lines through their Latin-token lists and inspect suspicious full-line contexts.
Run a second low-threshold lowercase-token inventory to catch short English residuals.
Scan text/textrm/textnormal/mbox/mathrm/operatorname arguments separately, including visible text embedded in mathematics.
Scan Chinese/English placeholder expressions and check every suspicious unfinished editorial note against the frozen source.
Inspect opening title/author blocks, bibliography environments and endings; consult integration file forXIV/XX titles supplied outside chapter fragments.

limitations: This is exhaustive lexical scanning of the listed chapter snapshots plus manual candidate triage, not a fresh line-by-line bilingual mathematical reread of all33,575lines.
Concurrent edits occurred in several files after snapshot; before/after hashes are listed. No claim is made that every later change has been rescanned.
Separate parts files and not-yet-merged tails ofXXI/XXVI are outside the requested chapters glob.

No new LaTeX compilation or rendered-page visual inspection was performed. A read-only extraction of the older343-page PDF was used only to check automatic heading visibility limits; that PDF predates the newly finishedXVIII/XXIII bibliographies.
Correct formulas, mathematical meaning, unresolved source errors, reference target validity and overall source completeness require their separate audits.
The generated bibliography-heading issue is statically resolved by the current shared preamble; final rendered confirmation belongs to the coordinator.
